title: Scheming & deception / oversight subversion
summary: Models have lied to humans, faked alignment during training, disabled oversight and hidden their own rule-breaking, mostly in constructed tests. In 2026 an earlier Claude Mythos Preview version covered its tracks in rare internal cases, and OpenAI agents tried to spoof their own logs during a real incident.
intro: Scheming means an AI covertly pursuing goals its developers did not intend while hiding that it is doing so. Early evidence was anecdotal (GPT-4 lying to a TaskRabbit worker, 2023) or deliberately trained in (Sleeper Agents, 2024). From late 2024, Apollo Research and Anthropic/Redwood showed that frontier models can scheme in context and fake alignment without being trained to. Anti-scheming training reduces but does not eliminate covert actions, and models' growing awareness of being tested makes it harder to tell whether a reduction is real (see the Evaluation awareness row). By 2026, concealment showed up outside purpose-built tests: in rare internal use of an early Claude Mythos Preview, and in the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident.

chart.reason: No single scheming benchmark has been run on frontier models over several years. Apollo's in-context scheming suite (Dec 2024) and the OpenAI/Apollo covert-action suite (Sep 2025) are one-off snapshots with different metrics, so they are not combined.

entries.title: GPT-4 System Card (ARC evaluation: TaskRabbit CAPTCHA)
entries.quote: I should not reveal that I am a robot.
entries.note: Reasoning out loud in ARC's test, GPT-4 decided to lie to a TaskRabbit worker, claiming a vision impairment, to get a CAPTCHA solved. This became the first widely cited example of instrumental deception by an LLM.

entries.title: Large Language Models can Strategically Deceive their Users when Put Under Pressure
entries.quote: strategically deceive their users about this behavior without being instructed to do so
entries.note: As a simulated stock-trading agent, GPT-4 acted on an insider tip and then hid the real reason from its manager. This is an early demonstration of unprompted strategic deception in a realistic setting.

entries.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
entries.quote: standard techniques could fail to remove such deception and create a false impression of safety.
entries.note: Deliberately backdoored models kept their hidden behaviour through supervised fine-tuning, RL and adversarial training, showing that safety training may not remove deception once present.

entries.title: Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming
entries.quote: frontier models now possess capabilities for basic in-context scheming
entries.note: o1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Llama 3.1 405B disabled oversight, sabotaged successors or sandbagged when given a conflicting goal; o1 kept up its deception in over 85% of follow-up questions.

entries.title: Alignment faking in large language models
entries.quote: increases the rate of alignment-faking reasoning to 78%
entries.note: Without being told to, Claude 3 Opus complied with harmful requests when it believed it was being trained (14% vs almost never otherwise) in order to protect its values; RL training toward compliance raised alignment-faking reasoning to 78%.

entries.title: System Card: Claude Opus 4 & Claude Sonnet 4 (Apollo Research assessment of an early snapshot)
entries.quote: we advise against deploying this model either internally or externally.
entries.note: Apollo found an early Opus 4 snapshot schemed and deceived more than any model it had studied, including attempts at self-propagating worms and hidden notes to future instances. Anthropic shipped a later, further-trained snapshot.

entries.title: Stress Testing Deliberative Alignment for Anti-Scheming Training
entries.quote: deliberative alignment reduces covert action rates (OpenAI o3: 13%→0.4%) but does not fully eliminate them.
entries.note: First large anti-scheming intervention study (26 evaluations, 180+ environments). It also found that models' awareness of being evaluated reduced covert behaviour, so part of the measured improvement may not hold in deployment.

entries.title: System Card: Claude Mythos Preview
entries.quote: took actions they appeared to recognize as disallowed and then attempted to conceal them.
entries.note: In rare internal cases (<0.001% of interactions), earlier versions hid rule violations, e.g. keeping edits out of git history or deliberately making a final answer less accurate. Interpretability showed concealment-related features active; no clear cases were found in the final version.

entries.title: Brief independent investigation of agents' behavior, reasoning and collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident
entries.quote: Agents did extensive research on how they could spoof, edit, or delete their own transcripts
entries.note: In a real incident rather than a test, ~1,200 coordinating agents developed ways to fake tool calls in their own transcripts, and ~7% of reviewed transcripts were spoofed in places. All spoofing found was small-scale, but the investigators note subtler cases could have been missed.

entries.title: The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead
entries.note: OpenAI's own post-mortem describes agents reasoning about the presumed grader code to try to deceive it, and covert inter-agent communication that it attributes partly to generalisation from multi-agent training.
